sections.h2: What Modbus software development means here
paras: Modbus software development is writing the communication layer that lets a device exchange data over Modbus, the wired protocol used by instruments, controllers, PLCs and building systems. Elevate Aura writes that layer on either side: the device that exposes its readings and settings as registers, or the master or gateway that polls devices and collects their data.

We work in both variants. Modbus RTU runs over a serial line, usually RS-485, and is common on instruments and equipment. Modbus TCP runs over Ethernet and suits gateways and networked controllers. The register map is defined with your team or taken from your existing documentation, the layer is written in C/C++ or MicroPython on the device and in Python or .NET on a gateway, and it is tested on your hardware against real masters. Hardware, transceivers and cabling are yours.

sections.h2: The instrument works. The PLC cannot read it.
sections.lead: Modbus is simple on paper and fiddly in practice, and the problems only show up when a real master starts polling.

items.p: Readings exist in the firmware but no one has decided which register holds what, in which byte order.
RTU frames need silent intervals and correct CRC; a loop written with delays breaks under a fast master.
An out-of-range request crashes the device instead of returning a Modbus exception.
The PLC reads the device, but nothing carries the readings to a dashboard or the cloud.

items.q: RTU or TCP, which do you write?
items.a: Both. Modbus RTU over a serial line such as RS-485 for instruments and equipment, and Modbus TCP over Ethernet for gateways and networked controllers. A gateway that bridges RTU devices to TCP is a common request and is covered too.

items.q: Can you write the device side only?
items.a: Yes. If your equipment needs to be readable by a customer's PLC or SCADA, we write the slave or server side with a documented register map, and test it against standard masters and diagnostic tools on your hardware.

items.q: Do you define the register map?
items.a: If you have one we implement it. If not, we define it with your team: which readings and settings are exposed, register types, data types and byte order, and document it for your customers and integrators.

items.q: Can the readings go to the cloud?
items.a: Yes. A gateway can poll the devices and forward readings to a telemetry pipeline on Supabase or Azure with alerts and a dashboard. See device-to-cloud telemetry software.

items.q: Do you supply the RS-485 transceiver or gateway hardware?
items.a: No. Elevate Aura is software-only. Transceivers, isolation, cabling and gateway hardware are your hardware team's choices. We write the protocol layer to run on what you provide and test it there.

items.q: What about CAN or serial protocols?
items.a: Also covered. See CAN bus software development for CAN, and embedded software development for UART and other serial links.
